chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Samanani, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade eating what the ant carries in its mouth and its legs.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet forbid regarding what ants carry?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib*, establishes a prohibition against consuming food items that are still attached to the carrier, such as grains held in an ant's mouth or legs, emphasizing the principle of *istihlak* (consumption) and purity in trade. It falls under the chapter of *al-Makasib* (earnings), highlighting the ethical dimensions of commercial transactions where the integrity of the commodity is maintained. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ensuring that goods sold are free from hidden impurities or excessive waste, thereby preserving the fairness of the exchange.
